answer: Payouts sit in a glacier lockbox thawing one slice per epoch, only while the owner emits a fresh live signal: a beacon-bound proof of fresh work, never replayable. Each signal must cross a mesh of three lottery-drawn strangers; each relay stakes a deposit, and one proven fake burns the mesh's deposits and refreezes the lockbox. A zephyr of random audits sweeps the mesh, so clones cannot hide. n clones need n lockboxes, n signals, n stranger meshes; strangers refuse lookalikes, and overlap between two clones' meshes freezes both, so fleet cost outruns n while honest payout stays flat.
